attribution: Swami Vivekananda; lectures given in New York
author: vivekananda
period: Lectures given around the winter of 1895–1896; published in 1896
summary: Vivekananda's lectures on the yoga of action: working without attachment as a path to freedom.
whyRead: It is a widely read modern account of karma yoga, drawing on the Gita and presenting unselfish work and service as a complete spiritual path. It is a modern exposition shaped by its setting and audience.
questions: How can work be a spiritual practice?
How do we act without being bound by results?

keyTeachings.title: Work as character formation
keyTeachings.text: Every action leaves impressions that shape character, so the way we work matters as much as what we achieve.

keyTeachings.title: Duty is relative
keyTeachings.text: Vivekananda argues that duty depends on one's position and circumstances, and that each is great in his own place.

keyTeachings.title: Non-attachment
keyTeachings.text: The core teaching is to work intensely but without attachment to results, the modern restatement of the Gita's nishkama karma.

keyTeachings.title: Service as worship
keyTeachings.text: Helping others is presented as helping oneself and, finally, as worship of the divine in them.

structure.label: Eight chapters in the common edition

relatedTexts.note: The classical source of karma yoga, for example Gita 2.47 and 3.35
